title: Cross-region watermark checkpointing for real-time billing deduplication
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Problem: our real-time billing pipeline can double-count token consumption when the same request is ingested in multiple regions (edge fanout, DR replays, or delayed reingestion). Root cause is lack of a coordinated, durable watermark/checkpointing scheme to mark 'committed' consumption ranges per tenant-route. This ticket introduces a lightweight cross-region checkpointing service and idempotent compaction stage to ensure single-source-of-truth for billing events without blocking real-time visibility.
design_summary: Introduce a Checkpoint Manager that emits monotonic watermarks per tenant+route. Consumers write provisional token events to the regional topic and periodically attempt to 'commit' ranges by proposing a checkpoint to the Checkpoint Manager. The compaction stage consults committed watermarks to collapse overlapping events and emit a single billed delta. Checkpoints are stored in a durable, highly-available KV store with optimistic concurrency control. To minimize latency, we use per-tenant sharding and local fast-path caching with background reconciliation.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): centralized checkpoint manager with per-tenant sharding — simpler correctness model and compact state, adds single service but horizontally scalable.
Option B: purely eventual dedupe via long retention + offline batch reconciliation — lower runtime complexity but delays billing accuracy and complicates credits/rollbacks.
Option C: embedding checkpoints in the ingestion topic using tombstone markers — avoids new service but requires coordinated topic compaction and complex consumer semantics across regions.
Rationale: we prioritize near-real-time correctness and predictable customer billing; central checkpointing with optimistic commits provides a pragmatic balance between latency and correctness.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate billed tokens for cross-region-replayed requests in 99.99% of simulated fanout scenarios (test harness).
End-to-end billing ingestion latency increase <= 150ms P95 compared to baseline for typical request rates (after warm cache).
Checkpoint manager scales to 10k tenants with median commit latency < 50ms under realistic load in staging.
Comprehensive unit & integration tests covering out-of-order events, duplicates, and late-arriving records.
Migration path and automatic reprocessing plan documented for historical streams older than 7 days.
tasks: Spec: define checkpoint protobuf and commit/inspect APIs (incl. tenant+route granularity).
Infra: provision KV store (HA cluster) and per-region cache layer; add KMS for checkpoint signing keys.
Consumer: instrument ingestion consumer to buffer provisional events and call commit protocol on watermark advances.
Compactor: implement compaction stage that consults committed watermarks and emits collapsed billing deltas to canonical topic.
Telemetry: add metrics for commit latency, commit conflicts, compaction ratio, and duplicate-detection rate.
E2E tests: build simulator to exercise cross-region fanout, DR replays, and delayed ingestion; verify no double billing.
Migration: author reprocessing job to reconcile last 30 days of events for opt-in tenants and run in sandbox before prod roll-out.
Docs & Runbook: update billing docs, create troubleshooting playbook for checkpoint conflicts and failed compactions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: single-service contention under hot-tenant patterns. Mitigation: tenant sharding with sticky routing and backpressure + capacity autoscale policy.
Risk: commit conflicts causing retries and higher latency. Mitigation: optimistic concurrency with exponential backoff and monitoring alerts for high conflict rates.
Risk: operator error during migration leading to re-billing. Mitigation: staged opt-in migration, dry-run mode, validation checks and manual approval gates.
implementation_notes: Use existing streaming infra (Kafka topics + consumer groups). Checkpoint Manager exposes gRPC and HTTP APIs, with protobuf schemas stored in schema-registry. Keep per-tenant checkpoint metadata small (last-committed-offset, checksum, timestamp, opaque metadata for debug). Signed checkpoint tokens allow downstream systems to validate commits without extra lookups.
